arxiv-2205-07755.title: Quantum Receiver Enhanced by Adaptive Learning
arxiv-2205-07755.creator: Chaohan Cui, William Horrocks, Shuhong Hao, Saikat Guha, N. Peyghambarian, Quntao Zhuang, Zheshen Zhang
arxiv-2205-07755.description: Abstract Quantum receivers aim to effectively navigate the vast quantum-state space to endow quantum information processing capabilities unmatched by classical receivers. To date, only a handful of quantum receivers have been constructed to tackle the problem of discriminating coherent states.

arxiv-2210-10296.title: The Modified Kähler-Ricci Flow, II
arxiv-2210-10296.creator: Haotian Wu, Zhou Zhang
arxiv-2210-10296.description: Abstract . We improve the understanding of both finite time and infinite time singularities of the modified Kähler-Ricci flow as initiated by the second author of this paper in [ 26 ] . This is done by relating the modified Kähler-Ricci flow with the recent studies on the classic Kähler-Ricci flow and the degenerate complex Monge-Ampère equation.

arxiv-2301-06160.title: TextileNet: A Material Taxonomy-based Fashion Textile Dataset
arxiv-2301-06160.creator: Shu Zhong, Miriam Ribul, Youngjun Cho, Marianna Obrist
arxiv-2301-06160.description: Abstract The rise of Machine Learning (ML) is gradually digitalizing and reshaping the fashion industry. Recent years have witnessed a number of fashion AI applications, for example, virtual try-ons. Textile material identification and categorization play a crucial role in the fashion textile sector, including fashion design, retails, and recycling.

arxiv-2307-08128.title: Minimal surfaces and Colding-Minicozzi entropy in complex hyperbolic space
arxiv-2307-08128.creator: Jacob Bernstein, Arunima Bhattacharya
arxiv-2307-08128.description: Abstract . We study notions of asymptotic regularity for a class of minimal submanifolds of complex hyperbolic space that includes minimal Lagrangian submanifolds. As an application, we show a relationship between an appropriate formulation of Colding-Minicozzi entropy and a quantity we call the C ​ R CR -volume that is computed from the asymptotic geometry of such submanifolds. 1.

arxiv-2404-03833.title: An ExplainableFair Framework for Prediction of Substance Use Disorder Treatment Completion* * Note: This manuscript has been accepted to the IEEE International Conference on Healthcare Informatics (IEEE ICHI 2024).
arxiv-2404-03833.creator: Mary M. Lucas 1 , Xiaoyang Wang 1 , Chia-Hsuan Chang 1 , Christopher C. Yang 1 , Jacqueline E. Braughton 2 , and Quyen M. Ngo 2
arxiv-2404-03833.description: Abstract Fairness of machine learning models in healthcare has drawn increasing attention from clinicians, researchers, and even at the highest level of government. On the other hand, the importance of developing and deploying interpretable or explainable models has been demonstrated, and is essential to increasing the trustworthiness and likelihood of adoption of these models.

arxiv-2404-18921.title: Anomaly and invertible field theory with higher-form symmetry: Extended group cohomology
arxiv-2404-18921.creator: Shi Chen
arxiv-2404-18921.description: Abstract In the realm of invertible symmetry, the topological approach based on classifying spaces dominates the classification of ’t Hooft anomalies and symmetry protected topological phases. We explore the alternative algebraic approach based on cochains that directly characterize the lattice lagrangian of invertible field theories and the anomalous phase factor of topological operator rearrangements.

arxiv-2501-14613.title: Improved algorithms and novel applications of the FrankWolfe.jl library
arxiv-2501-14613.creator: Mathieu Besançon mathieu.besancon@inria.fr, Sébastien Designolle designolle@zib.de, Jannis Halbey halbey@zib.de, Deborah Hendrych hendrych@zib.de, Dominik Kuzinowicz kuzinowicz@zib.de, Sebastian Pokutta pokutta@zib.de, Hannah Troppens troppens@zib.de, Daniel Viladrich Herrmannsdoerfer viladrich@zib.
arxiv-2501-14613.description: Abstract Frank-Wolfe (FW) algorithms have emerged as an essential class of methods for constrained optimization, especially on large-scale problems. In this paper, we summarize the algorithmic design choices and progress made in the last years of the development of FrankWolfe.jl, a Julia package gathering high-performance implementations of state-of-the-art FW variants.

arxiv-2510-22809.title: A Theory of the Mechanics of Information: Generalization Through Measurement of Uncertainty (Learning is Measuring)
arxiv-2510-22809.creator: Christopher J. Hazard, Michael Resnick, Jacob Beel, Jack Xia, Cade Mack, Dominic Glennie, Matthew Fulp, David Maze, Andrew Bassett, Martin Koistinen
arxiv-2510-22809.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Traditional machine learning relies on explicit models and domain assumptions, limiting flexibility and interpretability. We introduce a model-free framework using surprisal (information theoretic uncertainty) to directly analyze and perform inferences from raw data, eliminating distribution modeling, reducing bias, and enabling efficient updates including direct edits and deletion of training data.

britannica-1911-rate.title: Rate (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-rate.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-rate.description: Article 'Rate' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 22), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. rata, from pro rata parte, ratus being the participle of reri, to think, judge). In England the term is specially applied to the levying of public money contributions for local purposes, as distinguished from the “taxes” raised for what are treated as general state purposes.

pmc-11607236.title: RGB Color-Discriminable Photonic Synapse for Neuromorphic Vision System
pmc-11607236.creator: Bum Ho Jeong, Jaewon Lee, Miju Ku, Jongmin Lee, Dohyung Kim, Seokhyun Ham, Kyu-Tae Lee, Young-Beom Kim, Hui Joon Park
pmc-11607236.description: Highlights Photonic synapse capable of multispectral color discrimination is demonstrated.Strong excited-state dipoles enable remarkable discrimination intensity (0.05–40 mW cm-2).This approach is not restricted to a specific medium in the channel layer, and convolutional neural network with synapses array achieves over 94% inference accuracy for Canadian-Institute-For-Advanced-Research-10 images.Supplementary InformationThe online version contains supplementary material available at 10.1007/s40820-024-01579-y.

pmc-12420353.title: Perioperative Blood Management on a Successful Surgical Operation of a Patient With Congenital Coagulation Factor V Deficiency
pmc-12420353.creator: Ronghui Shi, Jianjun Wu, Qiang Meng, Ji Nie, Li Zhang, Xiaoqiong Long, Lan Yang, Shuming Zhao
pmc-12420353.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Thrombelastogram may provide a more accurate assessment of coagulation condition and transfusion strategy than the traditional coagulation profile and factor assays, and may be a useful ancillary tool guiding treatment decisions in factor V deficiency patients undergoing surgical procedures. Introduction Factor V (FV) deficiency, inherited or acquired, is a rare bleeding disease with an estimated prevalence of 1 per 1 million live births [1, 2].

pmc-12580297.title: The Impact Mechanism of Inter‐Basin Water Transfer on Fish Assemblages Was Revealed Using a Model of Terminal Reservoirs
pmc-12580297.creator: Zhenhao Cheng, Anxiang Wang, Yujing Cui, Lei Gao, Fei Cheng, Fengyue Shu, Songguang Xie
pmc-12580297.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Understanding the impact mechanism of inter‐basin water transfer projects (IBWTs) on fish assemblages is critical for conserving aquatic ecosystems and managing water transfer. However, direct evidence of the impact mechanism of IBWTs on fish assemblages is absent. Fish assemblages in newly built terminal reservoirs originate and assemble with diverted individuals through water transfer in IBWTs, providing a valuable model for mechanistic research.

pmc-12875768.title: Selection–diversification interplay in oligonucleotide chemical evolution
pmc-12875768.creator: Jiro Kakizaki, Ryo Mizuuchi
pmc-12875768.description: The emergence of catalytic RNAs (ribozymes) may have set the stage for an “RNA world” preceding protein evolution. The probability of ribozyme emergence and maintenance would have depended on available oligonucleotide compositions. Excessively high or low sequence diversity could hinder ribozyme formation, whereas balanced diversity is likely more favorable.

pmc-12984356.title: Limitations of Retrospective Machine Learning Models for Predicting Tracheostomy After Cardiac Surgery
pmc-12984356.creator: Felix Wiesmueller, Johannes Rösch, Stephan Kersting, Thomas Strecker
pmc-12984356.description: Background/Objectives: Early tracheostomy seems favorable in prolonged ventilated patients after surgery. Hence, predicting tracheostomy after cardiac surgery is essential. Recently proposed prediction models aim to support this decision-making process, but their diagnostic validity across other patient populations remains uncertain. Methods: A retrospective single-center study was performed at a university hospital.

pmc-13012227.title: Instagram Memes of Oral Nicotine Pouches: Content Analysis Study
pmc-13012227.creator: Samia Amin, Yunping Wu, Samantha Baptista, Scott K Okamoto, Thaddeus A Herzog, Crissy Terawaki Kawamoto, Pallav Pokhrel, Emmanuel Kusi Achampong
pmc-13012227.description: BackgroundOral nicotine pouches (ONPs), such as Zyn, have gained popularity among young people; however, their portrayal on social media remains under-studied. Instagram memes, a widely shared form of digital communication, may shape young people’s perceptions about ONPs and contribute to the widespread acceptance of ONP use.

pmc-13161028.title: Giant Cell Arteritis Following COVID-19 Vaccination: A Consumer-Stimulated Analysis
pmc-13161028.creator: Aishwarya N Shetty, John H Mallard, Daneeta Hennessy, Nicholas Wood, Hazel J Clothier, Jim P Buttery, the SAFESIG–GP Primary Health Network (PHN) Collaboration Group
pmc-13161028.description: IntroductionGiant cell arteritis (GCA) is an immune-mediated vasculitis of large and medium arteries, mainly affecting older adults. Prompted by a consumer concern, a few spontaneous reports after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) vaccination and Australian regulator signal, we investigated a possible association between GCA and vaccination.MethodsThis study analysed multiple data sources from January 2021 to September 2024.

pmc-13348517.title: The influence of pterygium size on corneal refractive properties and higher-order aberrations
pmc-13348517.creator: Jianqin Shen, Ying Chen, Yanghong Chen, Bingzhen Gou, Hongguang Cui
pmc-13348517.description: ObjectiveTo evaluate associations between pterygium size parameters and corneal refractive properties and higher-order aberrations (HOAs).MethodsIn 41 patients with unilateral pterygium, thickness, length, and width were measured by anterior segment optical coherence tomography(AS-OCT). Corneal refractive parameters, irregularity indices, and HOAs were assessed using Pentacam HR. Correlation analyses evaluated relationships between pterygium dimensions and corneal parameters.
